chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Usman, from Sama'ah who said:
I asked him about the woman when she dies, so he said: 'Her husband inserts his hand under her shirt up to the elbows.'
ai.seo_question: How does a husband wash his deceased wife according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of Sama'ah, specifies that the husband washes his deceased wife by inserting his hand under her garment up to the elbows, a ruling derived from the principle of modesty (haya) regarding the awrah. In Shia jurisprudence, this method balances the intimacy of the marital bond with the preservation of dignity, distinguishing it from the full exposure required for other relatives or the general public.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al Husayn Bin Usman, from Sama’at who said,
‘I asked about the woman when she dies. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Her husband would insert his hand under her shirt up to the elbows’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-Husayn ibn ‘Uthman from Sama‘ah who has said the following: “
I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman who dies. He (the Imam) said, ‘Her husband can reach out with his hand under her shirt up to the elbows.’”
